Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner-accused No.3 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.299/2022 of Bangarpet Police Station, pending on the file of Principal Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Bangarpet, Kolar District, KGF., registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant- Sri. Narayanaswamy.

entities.text: JMFC Court, Bangarpet, Kolar District, KGF
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri. Chethan A., learned Counsel for the petitioner and Sri. K. Rahul Rai, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent -State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.3.
She is innocent and law abiding citizen.
She has not committed any offences as alleged.
She has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
She is having reasonable apprehension of being arrested by the police.
Therefore, she is before this Court.
The father of the deceased lodged the first information making bald and general allegations against accused No.1, who is the husband of the deceased.
Accused No.1 and the deceased married on 25.08.2022.
It was a love marriage and against the wishes of the family members.
The petitioner was residing separately and he has no idea as to what had happened on the date of incident and why the deceased committed suicide.
There is absolutely no materials found against the petitioner for having committed any of the offences.
The petitioner is not required to be detained in custody for further investigation.
She is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition in the interest of justice.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offences.
She is the mother-in-law of the deceased and mother of accused No.1.
Accused Nos.1 to 3 were residing together where the deceased committed suicide by hanging, as she could not tolerate the ill-treatment meted to her by all the accused.
The informant made specific allegations regarding the cruelty.
The investigation is still at the initial stage.
The death of the deceased was within two months from the date of marriage.

Under such circumstances, if the petitioner is granted anticipatory bail, she may never turn up before the Investigating Officer and she may abscond or may commit similar offences, threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
Smt Dyavaramma vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54399371/
2 "Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"
My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegations made against the petitioner is of serious nature.
The petitioner is the mother-in-law of the deceased and mother of accused No.1.
The father of the deceased lodged the first information stating that the deceased was subjected to cruelty by accused Nos.1 to 3 and that is the reason she committed suicide by hanging.
Date of marriage of the deceased with accused No.1 was 25.08.2022 and she died on 07.11.2022.
Even though, learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner is residing separately, there are absolutely no material to substantiate the same.
The investigation is still under progress.
There is legal presumption against the accused and in favour of the prosecution, since the deceased died within two months from the date of marriage.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The criminal petition is dismissed.
